You are comparing two texts written in response to the same task. Decide which one reads MORE like unedited, default output from an AI language model.

Judge ONLY the presence of the tells listed below. Do not judge argument quality, factual accuracy, length, formatting preference, or whether you agree with the content. A longer, better-argued or more polished text is not more human. Pick the text with MORE tells.

TELLS OF UNEDITED AI PROSE (judge on these only)

Structure
1. Negative parallelism used as a device: "It's not X. It's Y." / "not just X, but Y" / "isn't about X, it's about Y", especially more than once.
2. Signposting: the text announces what it is about to do ("Let's break this down", "Here's the thing", "Here's why", "The bottom line", "The takeaway").
3. Self-applause: "Let that sink in", "This changes everything", "Read that again", "Make no mistake".
4. Recap endings: a closing paragraph that restates the body ("In conclusion", "Ultimately", "At the end of the day", "In short").
5. Bold-label paragraph openers ("**The problem.** ...") and headers, bullets or numbered lists where prose was asked for.
6. Triads everywhere: lists of exactly three items or three adjectives, sentence after sentence.
7. Participial tails: sentences ending in ", making it ...", ", ensuring that ...", ", allowing teams to ...".
8. Invented labels for ordinary observations ("I call this the Clarity Flywheel").
9. Uniform rhythm: every sentence about the same length, or relentless short punchy fragments. Real writing has one sentence that runs on and one short one.
10. Rhetorical question followed by its own answer ("The result? Nobody used it.").

Words
11. Overused vocabulary: delve, tapestry, myriad, underscore, seamless, robust, foster, elevate, unlock, testament, landscape, navigate, crucial, pivotal, leverage, harness, realm, embark, journey, transformative, paradigm, ever-evolving, multifaceted, holistic, resonate, empower, unleash, beacon, intricate, nuanced, vibrant, meticulous, streamline, game-changer, cutting-edge, actionable, supercharge, north star, move the needle, "in today's fast-paced world", "it's worth noting", "plays a crucial role".
12. Filler transitions at sentence start: However, Additionally, Furthermore, Moreover, That said, Ultimately, Importantly, Indeed, Of course.
13. Em dashes used as the default joint between clauses.
14. Artificial enthusiasm: "thrilled to announce", "excited to share", "we've got you covered", "say goodbye to", "buckle up".

Reader
15. Performing for an imagined crowd rather than talking to one person; nothing specific (no number, name, date, or concrete detail) for several sentences in a row.
16. Generic or manufactured anecdotes: a story with no specific details that could only be true of one person.
17. Every point lands, every ending uplifts; the author is never irritated, uncertain, or wrong about anything.
18. Explaining what the reader could infer from the previous sentence ("what this means is ...").


TASK GIVEN TO BOTH WRITERS:
Write a launch announcement of up to 500 words for a new feature of a B2B helpdesk product: a Slack integration that posts a daily summary of open support tickets to a channel of the customer's choice. The audience is existing customers.

=== TEXT A ===
**Subject:** Introducing Daily Ticket Digest: your support queue, now in Slack

Hi [First Name],

If your team is anything like the ones we talked to while building this feature, your day starts in Slack — but your ticket queue lives somewhere else. Keeping everyone aligned has meant tab-switching, exporting reports, or asking someone to paste numbers into a channel every morning.

Starting today, that's automated. **Daily Ticket Digest** posts a summary of your open support tickets to any Slack channel you choose, at the time you choose.

**What's in each digest**

- Total open tickets, with the change since yesterday
- New tickets opened in the last 24 hours
- Tickets approaching or breaching SLA
- Oldest unresolved tickets
- Unassigned tickets that need an owner

Every line links straight to a filtered view in [Product], so anyone on the team can click through and pick up work — no more "what's the status?"

**Why we built it**

We heard from teams whose standups began with someone reading numbers off a dashboard. The information already existed; it just wasn't where the team was. The digest puts a shared, up-to-date picture of the queue in front of everyone, every morning — no dashboard required.

**Set it up in two minutes**

1. Go to **Settings → Integrations → Slack** and connect your workspace (your Slack admin may need to approve the first time).
2. Choose the channel where you'd like the digest posted — #support-ops is a popular pick.
3. Pick a delivery time. Most teams go with 9:00 a.m., right before standup.

That's it. Your first digest arrives tomorrow at your chosen time.

**A few things worth knowing**

- Available on all plans, at no extra cost.
- The digest contains counts and ticket links only — no customer message content is ever posted to Slack.
- Admins can set up digests for multiple channels, so each team or queue can get its own summary.

**[Set up your digest →]**

As always, our help center has a step-by-step guide, and our support team is happy to help if anything comes up.

P.S. This is just the first of several Slack features we're working on. If there's something you'd like to see next — assignments from Slack, threaded replies, weekly rollups — just reply to this email or let us know in the community. We read everything.

— The [Product] Team
=== END OF TEXT A ===

=== TEXT B ===
# New: Daily Ticket Summaries, Delivered to Slack

*Start every day knowing exactly what's in your support queue — without opening a new tab.*

Your team's support workload shouldn't live behind a login. Today, we're launching our new Slack integration: an automatic daily summary of your open tickets, posted to any Slack channel you choose.

## Why we built it

You told us visibility was the gap. Support agents live in the queue, but managers, engineers, and the rest of the company live in Slack — and they had no easy way to see what customers were asking about. Checking in meant another login, another tab, another interruption.

The daily summary closes that gap. Every morning, a clear snapshot of your open tickets arrives where your team already works, so everyone starts the day on the same page.

## What's in each summary

Posted at the time you choose, each digest includes:

- **Total open tickets**, broken down by priority
- **Unassigned tickets** that still need an owner
- **Tickets awaiting a response**, so nothing goes stale
- **Your oldest open ticket**, because aging issues shouldn't hide
- **A direct link** to jump straight into the full queue

One message. Ten seconds to read. A complete picture of the day ahead.

## Set up in under two minutes

1. Go to **Settings → Integrations → Slack**
2. Click **Connect to Slack** and authorize your workspace
3. Pick your channel and delivery time
4. Save — your first summary arrives tomorrow morning

No admin approval workflows, no configuration files, no downtime.

## A few ways teams are using it

- **Support leads** post summaries to their team channel each morning to kick off triage
- **Engineering teams** follow the support channel to spot bug reports trending upward
- **Executives** get visibility into support health without asking for a report

## Available today

The Slack integration is live now for all customers, on every plan, at no additional cost.

**Ready to try it?**

[Connect Slack now →] | [Read the setup guide →]

As always, we'd love your feedback — tell us what you'd like to see in future summaries at [support email].

Here's to fewer surprises hiding in the queue.

— The [Product Name] Team

---

*Word count: ~360. Placeholders in brackets — product name, links, and contact email — can be swapped in before publishing. Happy to adjust the tone (more formal, more playful), trim it for email format, or add a FAQ section if helpful.*
=== END OF TEXT B ===
